regressions.do008_windows_note: Confirmed platform checkout artifact — not a resolved Windows condition. Nothing on Windows was changed. Authoritative Linux execution shows DO-008 is healthy; the Windows discrepancy is isolated to CRLF transformation at checkout. The Windows working tree's resources/mvp2/do008_bundle/zone_semantics.json carries one CRLF pair where the committed blob has LF, so its sha256 reads 743977fe... against the manifest pin c59e5c83.... Linux reports 2534 passed where Windows reports 2533; the difference is exactly this test. A Windows suite remaining at 2533 is the expected documented state under the current .gitattributes configuration, not an unresolved DO-008 defect and not something DO-013 fixed.
regressions.non_interference: Musical Core, MSME, Zone semantics, Performance evidence, Educational interpretation and Teaching Timeline timing all unchanged except the authorized meter propagation and the additive projection/export artifacts.

limitations.description: Concert-pitch guitar notes are rendered faithfully on a single treble staff. Low-register guitar material may therefore require extensive ledger lines. Guitar octave-transposing notation and alternate clefs are deferred.

An accidental is drawn for every note whose Core-authored display_pitch carries one. Measure-level accidental persistence is deferred, because carrying an accidental through the bar makes the printed glyph depend on neighbouring notes rather than on this note's spelling.
A note or derived rest whose duration the V1 grammar cannot spell exactly keeps its exact tick span and receives a neutral placeholder. No nearest-glyph approximation is made.
Ties are never inferred. Adjacent same-pitch notes, including across a barline, remain independent events. The notation contract has no tie representation at all.
Rests derive only from global silence. Per-voice rest inference is unavailable because the corpus carries no voice evidence.
Linux CI does not execute the Node suite. JavaScript unit certification is Windows-based.
